headlines.title: Global Market: Japan stocks slide as oil spike and rising bond yields weigh on sentiment
US-Japan Intervention Impact on Yen Demonstrates Strength, Says Gareth Berry
Japanese Yen remains near two-week low against US Dollar despite hawkish BoJ bets
Asia shares decline as worries about rising oil prices outweigh perks from strong earnings
Asia shares decline as worries about rising oil prices outweigh perks from strong earnings
Japan's Nikkei slides as Middle East stalemate fuels oil, inflation concerns

marketTone.ko: 일본 증시는 유가 급등과 채권 금리 상승 압력으로 인해 투자 심리가 위축되며 하락세를 보였습니다. 특히 중동 정세 불안으로 인한 유가 및 인플레이션 우려가 니케이 지수 하락을 주도했습니다. 한편, 엔화는 미국과의 개입 효과 및 일본은행의 매파적 전망에도 불구하고 미 달러 대비 2주래 최저치 부근에서 약세를 지속하며 압력을 받았습니다.
marketTone.en: Japanese stocks slid today, reflecting a broader decline across Asia, as sentiment was dampened by a spike in oil prices and rising bond yields. The Nikkei's decline was particularly driven by concerns over inflation, exacerbated by the Middle East stalemate and its impact on oil prices. Concurrently, the Japanese Yen remained under pressure, trading near a two-week low against the US Dollar, despite previous intervention efforts and hawkish Bank of Japan expectations.
